articles.title: Writing an OOTDBuy custom order for a hard-to-import listing
articles.description: OOTDBUY offers a custom order option for items you cannot locate through its normal product search.

sections.heading: Identify the item precisely
paragraphs: OOTDBUY offers a custom order option for items you cannot locate through its normal product search. Start with the original seller link and the variation you want to buy. A screenshot helps show what you mean, but the image alone cannot identify the current offer, distinguish two sellers using the same photo or tell the agent whether your preferred variant is available.

sections.heading: Describe the option in the seller's language
paragraphs: Copy the exact option label and add an English explanation if helpful. Include the color, size, quantity and any component that affects the product. For an organizer sold in stacked sections, describe which sections you need and how many. If the seller uses codes such as A and B, keep the code next to its photo. Mixing a translated description from one option with the image of another creates avoidable confusion.

sections.heading: Set instructions for a substitution
paragraphs: Decide in advance whether you would accept an alternative. For a coordinated set, a different shade might defeat the reason for buying. For a replaceable storage bin, a different color might be fine if the dimensions agree. Put the condition in plain language. If availability or price changes, ask the agent to contact you before a substitute is purchased.

sections.heading: Review the proposed order
paragraphs: Before paying, compare the seller link, chosen variant, number of units, item price and any domestic transport charge against your request. Look for warning signs such as a selected sample instead of a full-size product. Save the confirmed record and use it when the warehouse receives the goods. A complete custom order gives you an objective comparison if something unexpected arrives.

sections.heading: Specify a fallback only if you really want one
paragraphs: Custom ordering introduces a human reading your instructions. Give that person a decision they can carry out if the listing changes. “Please confirm with me if the listed black version is unavailable” is clear. “Black preferred, any dark color if necessary” gives broader permission. For a gift intended to match a set, those two requests could produce very different results. Put the instruction next to the variant and keep special requests separate from ordinary seller options. A written preference for a removable part cannot make a seller include one absent from the offer.

When the price is unclear, ask the agent to confirm the current item cost plus the seller's domestic charge before purchase. A seller could offer a deposit, sample or full product on one page. Record which one your request describes. If an agent asks for a higher amount, compare that new number with the intended option and ask why it changed. The answer might reveal a change of quantity or a separate charge rather than an increase in the unit price.

sections.heading: A worked custom-order brief
paragraphs: Imagine a carpenter needs two matte-black handles at a specific mounting distance. A usable brief names the original seller link, selected model, hole spacing, finish, unit count and whether mounting screws are included. It adds that the glossy version and a different spacing would not fit. If the seller uses labels B1 and B2, attach the screenshot showing the B2 option. When the order is ready, check the product page and the actual purchase screen against those six facts. Later, a warehouse photo with a ruler between the mounting holes will address a real installation question.

sections.heading: Make a custom request when the link opens to the wrong version
paragraphs: A seller link can open successfully and still be unsuitable for a normal order. It may show several similar variants under one image, require a size in the order notes, or display the option you selected only inside the marketplace app. Start by copying the visible product and seller identifiers from the source page. Save an image showing the active option, not just the attractive product photo at the top. If the platform can import the offer normally once the correct link is used, examine that route before submitting a second order for the same goods.

For a custom request, explain the reason briefly. For example, the standard product form loads a generic blank organizer, but the seller offers a version with three specific compartment sizes. This helps the agent understand which difference prompted the manual request. If the seller supplies a separate option code or diagram, attach it. A photo of the finished organizer might show the pattern, while the diagram gives the dimensions that determine whether your tools fit.

sections.heading: Handle notes that the seller must agree to
paragraphs: Some details simply identify a listed version; others ask the seller to change what they normally provide. Selecting a stated matte-black finish is a variant choice. Asking the seller to cut the part shorter or supply a different fixing is a special request that may affect price or returns. Put those requirements in separate sentences and ask the agent to obtain explicit seller confirmation before proceeding. A note typed into a custom form does not establish that the seller has accepted it.

Personalization requires particular care. If a product can carry a name or message, write the final text exactly once and clearly identify it as the text to reproduce. Check capitalization, spacing and any proof supplied before approval. Ask whether the seller can provide a preview and how a buyer error or production error would be handled. If the item must be usable even without the personalization, say whether you would accept the standard version. The agent should not need to guess which compromise you would prefer.

sections.heading: Compare the seller's reply against the original requirement
paragraphs: Keep the original request in view when the agent returns with a price or seller message. Read what has been confirmed and what remains unanswered. “Available in black” addresses color but says nothing about mounting distance, material or the number of pieces. A precise follow-up might ask, “Please confirm the centre-to-centre spacing for option B2 and whether this price buys two handles.” Two specific questions are easier to verify than an instruction to double-check everything.

When the seller proposes another option, ask which specification changes. A polished handle with the same mount may fit mechanically while looking wrong beside existing hardware. A visually identical piece with different hole spacing may be impossible to install. If you cannot accept a substitute that changes the critical feature, state that before payment. If multiple variants would work, list them in preference order, each with the seller's exact label. Retain the confirmed choice for the warehouse comparison.

sections.heading: Review the received goods as a custom-order customer
paragraphs: The evidence for a standard product may consist of a single order line. A custom order can depend on the original seller listing, the variant image, a message confirming a modification and the final agent order. Keep those together under one reference. At warehouse intake, identify what can be checked visually and what requires a measurement or specific photo. A front photo might confirm finish and count, while a rear view with a ruler could confirm mounting distance.

If the item differs, describe the exact confirmed requirement that was missed. Attach the confirmation and a photo showing the received feature. Ask what remedy is available before including the item in an international shipment. If it matches, record the final product identifier and confirmed specification for future use. Before repeating the order months later, check that the seller still supplies the same version. An archived custom request is a useful reference point, not proof that an old configuration remains available.

sections.heading: Keep manual and standard purchases distinct
paragraphs: When a failed import briefly added something to your cart, look for that old entry before paying for the custom version. Compare order identifiers and remove or leave unsubmitted the obsolete choice as appropriate. A duplicate order can appear plausible if the default option shares the same lead image as your intended custom product. Checking the cart against your requested quantity takes less effort than resolving two seller purchases after dispatch.

sections.heading: A brief for products sold in left and right versions
paragraphs: For an asymmetric part, describe orientation from a fixed reference point. The left bracket as viewed from the front of a cabinet can be the right one as viewed from behind it. If the seller supplies a labelled drawing, cite its part number and mark the required piece on a copy. Confirm whether the price buys one bracket or a matched pair. Those two details can matter more than the finish when the item is intended to fit existing hardware.

articles.title: Preparing an OOTDBuy forwarding order for a purchase you made yourself
articles.description: OOTDBUY describes forwarding as receiving packages sent to its warehouse and arranging their journey abroad.

sections.heading: Decide who will purchase the goods
paragraphs: OOTDBUY describes forwarding as receiving packages sent to its warehouse and arranging their journey abroad. This suits a different situation from asking an agent to buy something. If you have already paid the seller yourself, start by finding the forwarding instructions in your account. A second purchase order could result in two separate transactions for the same item.

sections.heading: Copy current warehouse details
paragraphs: Use the recipient details, address and any identifying instructions that OOTDBUY supplies for your parcel. Reusing an old screenshot can cause errors if the address or matching instructions changed. Confirm that the seller can enter every required field, including any unit or recipient code. Keep this correspondence in the private order channel. A public spreadsheet is a poor place to store identifying delivery information.

sections.heading: Reconcile a split seller shipment
paragraphs: If a seller dispatches a lamp shade and its stand in separate cartons, keep both domestic tracking references. Record which goods each box is supposed to contain and when each was sent. Ask OOTDBUY how to associate multiple arriving parcels with the forwarding entry. One warehouse arrival may settle only half the inventory, even when the seller treated the purchase as one order.

sections.heading: Keep the seller receipt available
paragraphs: Because you purchased the goods yourself, retain the original transaction record, seller messages and variant selections. If the wrong part arrives, the agent may be able to document what it received, while your seller account contains the original agreement. Ask which inspection and aftersales services apply to forwarding orders. Confirm all pieces are accounted for before arranging their international shipment.

sections.heading: Set expectations before the seller posts the parcel
paragraphs: Forwarding has two independent relationships. Your purchase agreement is with the original seller, while the international dispatch will involve OOTDBUY once the goods reach its warehouse. Check the seller's own aftersales and timing while you still control the purchase directly. Then check OOTDBUY's forwarding instructions for acceptance, matching and outward shipping. If the product needs special packing or a particular line, ask about it in advance. A successful domestic delivery alone cannot establish that every international route will accept the goods.

Suppose a seller offers a fragile desktop organizer only in a presentation box. Ask how they plan to protect the presentation box for the domestic leg. If it arrives crushed, the photograph and packaging history may matter to the seller. Ask what inspection is available on the forwarding service, including whether opening a sealed carton would affect seller remedies. Decide what to preserve before the domestic shipment leaves the seller, while changes to packing can still be requested.

sections.heading: Resolve an unmatched domestic delivery
paragraphs: A carrier receipt may show the warehouse address without linking the parcel to your account. Match the seller order, recipient information and carrier tracking before raising an enquiry. Send the relevant forwarding record and identify exactly when the carrier marked delivery. If two boxes came from the same shop, include both numbers and say which one is already visible. This prevents a previously matched box from being confused with the missing one. When the warehouse confirms the match, verify the contents list and deadline on the actual record.

sections.heading: Verify the receiving instructions field by field
paragraphs: When forwarding a self-purchased item, the marketplace seller needs an accurate domestic destination. Read the current OOTDBUY instructions and copy each field into the corresponding field used by the seller. A province, city, district, street address and warehouse identifier can be distributed differently across two forms. Check the final rendered address after saving it. Some forms may split long text or present a shortened preview; confirm that identifying information still appears in the actual order.

If the seller asks for a telephone number or recipient name, use the information the warehouse instructs you to supply for that forwarding transaction. Avoid substituting an old number from a public post or reusing another buyer's account-specific details. When the instructions are unclear, ask OOTDBUY before asking the seller to dispatch. Once the package is moving, an incorrect unit or identifying code can be harder to correct than an unsubmitted address entry.

sections.heading: Build a record of what the seller agreed to send
paragraphs: Forwarding begins after your own purchase decision, so retain the seller evidence independently of the agent's warehouse record. For each purchased unit, save the option text, seller identity, source purchase reference and quantity. If the seller promised to include an accessory outside the normal listing, preserve the message that confirms it. If several items are packed together, ask for a simple packing summary showing the expected contents. This gives you a baseline before the warehouse can confirm any physical receipt.

For illustration, a buyer purchases a desk lamp body, a separate stand and a detachable shade. The seller sends the shade in one carton and the body and stand together in another. The buyer needs three expected items, two domestic tracking numbers and eventually one or more international parcel numbers. If the records show only “lamp,” the first received carton can appear to satisfy the entire purchase. Name the components before the goods travel and mark each one received only when there is suitable evidence.

sections.heading: Investigate damage at the right stage
paragraphs: If a forwarded package reaches the warehouse visibly damaged, identify whether the problem concerns the outer carton, retail packaging or the goods themselves. Ask what photos or inspection the warehouse can provide within its forwarding service. Compare the new photos with any images the seller sent before domestic dispatch. If the seller packed a fragile item loosely, the before-and-after record matters to that seller relationship, while the agent can report only what it received and observed.

Avoid ordering overseas shipment simply to see the goods in person when a seller remedy may depend on their remaining in China. Ask the seller and the agent what options apply to the actual status and who would arrange any domestic return. If opening the box would affect a seal, warranty evidence or seller eligibility, ask before requesting that step. Separate the need to identify physical damage from the choice of remedy; you may need more information to make either decision.

sections.heading: Move from domestic intake to overseas dispatch
paragraphs: After all expected cartons are matched, decide how the contents should travel internationally. The seller's domestic carton may have been adequate for a short local journey but may need a different arrangement for the next stage. Tell the warehouse which original packaging has value to you, what should stay together and which pieces need additional separation. Ask for actual packed dimensions and route availability corresponding to the proposed arrangement. Compare those facts with your destination and budget.

Save a mapping from each seller order and domestic tracking number to the resulting international parcel. If the goods are combined with agent-purchased orders, retain which items you bought yourself. A later issue concerning the original seller's specification may need to be addressed through your own marketplace account. A later issue concerning a delivered international carton may need the parcel and carrier records instead. Keeping both relationships visible is one of the main practical advantages of a clean forwarding record.

sections.heading: Confirm what remains unresolved
paragraphs: Before marking the forwarding job complete, review any open question about missing parts, damage, required documents or outstanding seller payments. A domestic tracking result that says delivered does not answer any of those questions. Close the record when the goods have been matched and you have made an informed choice about their next shipment or remedy. If one carton remains unresolved, name it explicitly even when the rest of the order can move ahead.

sections.heading: When two sellers use the same marketplace platform
paragraphs: Create a separate forwarding note for each seller even if you placed both orders on the same marketplace account. Store names, purchased variants and tracking numbers can be similar, particularly with common household items. Label the expected cartons before any arrive. If one seller supplies the wrong part, the correct record lets you raise the issue with the seller that actually handled that transaction while leaving the other purchase and its forwarding plan intact.

articles.title: Checking an OOTDBuy outfit spreadsheet for missing pieces
articles.description: An outfit photo is a styling suggestion until the selected variant identifies what the seller supplies.

sections.heading: Read the offer one piece at a time
paragraphs: An outfit photo is a styling suggestion until the selected variant identifies what the seller supplies. A spreadsheet row can show a coordinated look while linking to one jacket, one skirt or a choice between them. In the live listing, map each visible piece to an exact option. Write “display only” beside anything that appears solely in the mood photos.

sections.heading: Compare sizes independently
paragraphs: A two-piece look can pair a loose top with a fitted bottom. Measure a similar top and bottom that you own and compare the seller's dimensions separately. If a single size selection controls the entire set, determine whether both pieces will work in that size. For a gift, write down the actual garment measurements available from the seller so the recipient can compare them without relying on one letter.

sections.heading: Check whether the colors can reasonably match
paragraphs: Matching shade names from different sellers can describe noticeably different fabrics. Look for photos showing both pieces together and compare the material descriptions, surface finish and lighting. If a precise match matters, ask whether both pieces come from the same listing or production option. Two separate warehouse photographs under different light will leave the comparison uncertain.

sections.heading: Build a buyable shortlist
paragraphs: For each outfit, keep the links, unit counts, required sizes, total merchandise cost and decision still open. A useful shortlist might show that a slightly more expensive bundle includes both pieces while the cheaper row links only to the top. Check the complete selected offer once more on OOTDBUY before payment, especially if you opened several similar colors in separate tabs.

sections.heading: Compare looks using a complete purchase budget
paragraphs: Start with the wardrobe gap you want to fill. An outfit consisting of trousers and a vest may use shoes and a shirt that you already own. Mark those as existing pieces so you do not add their cost or shipping weight to a new purchase. Now list the pieces you actually need. For a complete seller set, read whether stock or size choices are linked. If the jacket and trousers are separate, confirm each is available in the chosen size before committing to one half of a look you would only wear together.

Consider two hypothetical rows. One shows a jacket for 90 units and trousers for 75. Another offers a two-piece bundle for 150. The first costs 165 for both before domestic and overseas freight, but you may be able to choose two different sizes. The bundle saves 15 on merchandise yet could leave you with trousers you will not wear. A worthwhile comparison includes both the price and the conditions under which each outfit works.

sections.heading: Make repeated photos earn their place
paragraphs: When browsing independent OOTDBuy outfit sheets, similar styled images often dominate the first screen. Open a candidate only if you can identify a meaningful difference worth checking: a separate size selection, an included lining, a different waistband or a seller photo of the reverse. Save notes under those differences rather than accumulating near-identical images. For color coordination, look at the texture and finish as well as the shade. If matching is essential, prioritize evidence of both pieces in the same light and ask the seller what was used in the photograph.

sections.heading: Use the outfit photograph to identify individual design details
paragraphs: Begin with the part of the image that drew your attention. It may be the cropped length of the jacket, a high waist on the trousers or the way the two fabrics reflect light. Identify which of those properties the seller actually describes. A styled pose can make a regular-length shirt appear cropped or conceal the shape of the waistband. Look for a flat view, a rear view and the dimensions associated with the selected option before deciding whether the item reproduces the feature you want.

If a belt, scarf or removable trim is visually central to the look, check whether it is part of the product. The outfit photograph may include an accessory sold elsewhere. An option saying skirt with belt can mean something quite different from a skirt whose styling image happens to include a belt. Write the accessory on the shortlist only when the option or seller documents it. If you already own a suitable substitute, mark that explicitly so you are not comparing a supposedly complete set against a look that depends on an unpriced extra.

sections.heading: Compare the proportions of the pieces together
paragraphs: For garments intended to overlap, dimensions combine. A fitted top might end exactly where one pair of high-rise trousers begins but leave a gap over a lower-rise pair. Measure the length of a reference top and the rise of trousers that you already wear together. Compare the proposed pieces using the same endpoints and think about movement, sitting and layers. The model's height or pose provides much less direct information than dimensions tied to a garment you can actually try at home.

Consider a jacket that is intended to sit above the waistband. A roomier size could add the chest space you need yet also change the length or sleeve position. If a shared set size would solve the jacket issue while making the trousers too loose, check whether the seller offers separately selectable sizes. If another seller sells the two pieces independently, compare their fabrics and color evidence as well as their sizes. A better numerical fit can come with a greater risk of poor visual coordination.

sections.heading: Recognize when a row points to a look rather than a buyable item
paragraphs: Some independent spreadsheet entries describe a type of outfit and use a broad image to help people browse. Follow the source and identify exactly what can be added at the selected price. When several options look similar, keep an item-by-item checklist with the live link, seller, variant, quantity and delivered decision still needed. If the listing points only to a jacket, link the matching trousers separately or mark the look incomplete. A shortlist that admits a missing piece is more useful than a polished picture that hides it.

For repeated listings, look for evidence that the products really differ. The same styling image can appear with different materials, linings or construction. A close-up of a seam, a fabric label or a size diagram from the seller can clarify a decision. Where all candidate pages repeat the same images without supplying the specification you need, ask a focused question or choose a better documented alternative. Ranking the pages solely by the lowest visible price can reward an accessory option or the wrong quantity.

sections.heading: Plan the warehouse review around the outfit
paragraphs: When the pieces arrive, check each item's own label and warehouse photo against its order. Then look at the relationship between them: whether the intended colors appear compatible, whether the actual waist and hem measurements allow the overlap you expected, and whether all promised accessories are present. If a color match is essential, ask whether a photo of both received pieces under the same light is possible and whether there is a fee. A comparison across unrelated lighting setups will leave more uncertainty.

If one piece is unavailable, decide whether the rest still serves a purpose. A useful neutral jacket might be worth keeping even when the coordinating skirt is canceled; a highly specific patterned top may lose its appeal without the matching bottom. Check any return or storage deadline before waiting for the missing piece. Having a fallback outfit in mind lets you decide based on what you will actually wear and what the available seller terms permit, instead of buying another near-match to rescue an uncertain original choice.

sections.heading: For a look assembled across seasons
paragraphs: A seller might still offer last season's trousers alongside a newly produced jacket with a similar shade name. Ask whether the pieces are sold as a matching set and whether the seller can show the actual variants together. If exact matching is less important than a coordinated look, choose a deliberate difference in tone or texture and make that your selection criterion. This can be more reliable than paying for two pieces whose supposed color match rests on unrelated photographs.

articles.title: How to compare OOTDBuy shipping estimates for a mixed parcel
articles.description: The OOTDBUY shipping calculator is a starting point for comparing a particular parcel.

sections.heading: Write down the shipment you are pricing
paragraphs: The OOTDBUY shipping calculator is a starting point for comparing a particular parcel. Use a destination, contents list and packing assumption that you can reproduce. A pair of shoes in its retail box occupies different space from the same pair packed without it. Specify which version you want before interpreting the quote.

sections.heading: Separate exclusions from price differences
paragraphs: Two search results may represent different services or different rules for accepting the goods. Read the line's instructions for the destination and the actual contents. If a route appears for an ordinary shirt but disappears when you add another item category, ask which restriction applies. Changing the declared description to obtain a quote would leave you with an estimate for a different parcel.

sections.heading: Test a useful packing change
paragraphs: Suppose a carton measures 30 by 20 by 20 centimetres. A second carton with the same base and a 30-centimetre height occupies fifty percent more space. That arithmetic illustrates the effect of a tall item on packed volume. It does not predict the rate. Re-run the calculator with the relevant measurements, keep the actual weight consistent where appropriate, and note whether the available routes or charges change.

sections.heading: Choose a defensible comparison
paragraphs: Save the date, route name, estimated charge and what the quote includes. Put any optional protection or packing service on its own line. When the warehouse provides the packed figures, compare them with the saved assumptions. The answer may be a change in dimensions, service or contents. A single screenshot of the cheapest amount without its inputs cannot tell you which.

sections.heading: Read volumetric figures as route-specific numbers
paragraphs: Some shipping comparisons use the space a carton occupies as well as its mass. Look for the divisor, units and rounding instructions on the actual line. As a fictional example only, suppose a carrier uses cubic centimetres divided by 5,000. A carton measuring 40 by 25 by 20 centimetres gives 20,000 cubic centimetres, or four kilograms under that particular rule. If another option has a different divisor, you cannot transfer the four-kilogram result to it without calculating again. The live service description decides whether the rule applies and which figure governs the charge.

Test the weight that matters to the shipment. A scale reading for loose goods excludes the carton and protective material. A seller's listed product weight may describe a sample size, one variant or a net weight without retail packaging. Keep each figure labelled by origin. If the quote changes once the warehouse weighs the packed box, compare the new gross weight with the old gross estimate before deciding the price change is an error.

sections.heading: Work through a mixed-item decision
paragraphs: Imagine combining a folded shirt, a rigid shoe box and a framed photograph. The shirt adds little structure; the frame determines a minimum footprint and needs padding; the shoe box can raise the stack. A quote for their combined weight in a small generic carton misses the geometry. Sketch possible arrangements and ask which protective approach the warehouse can actually provide. Price the viable arrangement and one realistic alternative. The best comparison is between two parcels you would really agree to ship.

sections.heading: Start with the contents the carrier will actually receive
paragraphs: List every item and whether it will remain in its retail packaging. Separate rigid, fragile and compressible pieces. The largest dimension of a rigid object may control the carton even if the object is light. A decorative panel 45 centimetres long cannot travel in a carton that measures only 40 centimetres internally unless it can safely be disassembled. Confirm whether disassembly is possible and acceptable rather than entering an idealized box that the warehouse cannot produce.

Include the protective arrangement in the description. For a framed print, the corners and front surface may need protection; for shoes intended as a gift, the retail box may need a second carton around it. Those choices can add both weight and space, but removing them changes the condition you expect on arrival. Build a quote for the protected outcome you actually want. If you are willing to accept a different level of packaging, price that as a second option and make the change visible in the comparison.

sections.heading: Distinguish a carrier's dimensional rule from your estimate
paragraphs: Carriers publish terminology for determining billable weight, and UPS, for example, explains dimensional calculations in its own shipping documentation. Use such guidance to understand the concept, then obtain the rule for the specific OOTDBUY line displayed for your destination. Do not assume that an international agent's quoted service uses the same divisor, units, price steps or minimums as a carrier's separate retail rate. Keep the calculation you used next to the quote so it can be checked.

A useful worksheet contains the actual packed mass, the measured external dimensions, the relevant dimensional formula if published and the resulting chargeable figure under that line's rules. If a required field is unknown, leave it marked unknown. A made-up number with several decimal places gives the appearance of precision without improving the decision. Instead run two realistic boundary cases, such as preserving or removing a nonessential outer sleeve, and see whether the available routes or quoted totals change.

sections.heading: Compare services with different inclusions
paragraphs: A lower base price may be attached to a line with different tracking coverage, packing restrictions or delivery assumptions. Read the offered service description and record which features matter to you. If the buyer needs a trackable delivery to a workplace, a quote that omits information needed by that workplace may deserve clarification before purchase. If the parcel contains a fragile gift, check what packing and compensation conditions apply to the chosen line before deciding how much the lowest quote is worth.

Put optional services in their own rows. A comparison should make clear whether one side contains protection and the other does not, whether a promotion actually applies, and what currency the amount represents. Where customs or taxes are mentioned, copy the route's actual wording and consult the relevant official guidance for the destination if you need a precise obligation. Avoid adding an assumed tax amount or promising coverage that the current route does not explicitly describe.

sections.heading: Explain a later difference using the saved inputs
paragraphs: Once the warehouse gives you a final packed quote, start by comparing the same four physical facts: actual weight and the three outside measurements. Then check route, destination, item category and selected services. If any changed, rerun the comparison using the new inputs and look for a matching explanation. For example, a taller box could bring a bulky item within a different pricing step or remove a smaller-parcel service entirely. The final quote may represent a different physical shipment from the one you originally imagined.

If you still cannot explain the difference, send the original calculation and the current parcel record to OOTDBUY with a short, specific question. Ask which value or service changed and whether an alternative packing arrangement is available. Keep the response with the final payment reference. The resulting record has more long-term value than a screenshot of a cheap quote because it can help you plan another shipment containing a similar rigid object, fragile component or retail carton.

sections.heading: Compare a shared carton against two separate shipments
paragraphs: If the mixed parcel produces an unexpected quote, price a second plan that isolates the item controlling the size or route. Add the two genuine separate quotes and compare them with the mixed total in the same currency, using equivalent service features where possible. Record which assumptions differ, including protection, destination and tracking. If the two shipments use different lines, include the actual service tradeoffs in the decision. A saving on paper can disappear when one parcel needs extra protection or a different delivery arrangement.

articles.title: Checking OOTDBuy shoe photos when the box and shoe labels differ
articles.description: An OOTDBuy inspection question about shoes is easier to resolve when you distinguish the carton label, the left shoe and the right shoe.

sections.heading: Identify which label belongs to what
paragraphs: An OOTDBuy inspection question about shoes is easier to resolve when you distinguish the carton label, the left shoe and the right shoe. Start with the seller's promised variant and size system. Keep the size exactly as written, including any regional designation or width code. A size number without its scale can lead two people to describe the same pair differently.

sections.heading: Build a small photo set
paragraphs: A wide shot establishes the pair and overall color. A separate view of each internal size label helps establish whether the shoes match each other. If you need the retail box, ask for a legible photo of its label as well. Reference a specific uncertainty, such as a different width printed on one shoe. A request for “better photos” leaves the warehouse guessing what information matters.

sections.heading: Interpret the discrepancy
paragraphs: If both shoe labels agree with the order but the carton label differs, decide whether the box itself matters to you and ask the agent to confirm the packing history. If the two shoes show different sizes, treat the pair as unresolved even if the carton matches. A seller size chart can help explain a conversion, but it cannot reconcile conflicting labels on the left and right shoes.

sections.heading: Decide before dispatch
paragraphs: Save the photos and order selection together. OOTDBUY lists inspection and aftersales guidance in its help topics. Ask through the specific order about available checks, seller remedies and timing. Avoid authorizing a combined overseas parcel until you know which pair will be included. A clear written record also helps if a replacement arrives under a similar warehouse description.

sections.heading: Read the size system and shape together
paragraphs: Shoe labels often display several regional sizes in a grid. First match the row headings, then compare the numbers. An image crop showing only one number can make a correct pair appear contradictory. Ask for enough of the label to see the size system, any width marking and the model code. Keep the left and right photos associated with the same warehouse record. For a pair intended to match an existing shoe, model, cut and width can matter as much as the number stamped inside.

If you need an internal length check, specify what is to be measured and ask what the warehouse can do without damaging the shoe. A removable insole laid flat can be measured from heel to toe along a defined line. External outsole length includes design features and usually answers a different question. A measurement along a curved insole and one straight across a photograph can also differ. Compare like measurements and ask for both endpoints to remain visible.

sections.heading: Build a decision from three outcomes
paragraphs: If the carton and shoes all identify the intended size, move on to visible condition and your personal fit questions. If both shoes agree with each other but the box differs, ask whether the carton was mixed up and whether the correct packaging is required. If the left and right labels genuinely conflict after matching the scale, request an order-specific review before shipping. A marketplace screenshot with one selected size is useful evidence, but it cannot settle which physical pair is in front of the photographer.

sections.heading: Distinguish a regional size conversion from a mismatched pair
paragraphs: A shoe may carry more than one size on the same label. Read the system headings and compare the corresponding entry on each shoe, rather than comparing two prominent numbers at different positions in two photos. A label photographed upside down or partly folded can hide the heading that explains the discrepancy. Ask for the whole label in focus and enough of the shoe to identify its side. Keep the selected seller option and its stated size scale beside the images.

Width and model codes can resolve an apparent match or reveal an overlooked issue. Two labels may show the same length size but different width designations. A similar-looking shoe in a different model can use a different last or construction. If width was a specific part of your order, identify its code in the seller description and ask the agent to compare that code. A generic reply that both shoes are the same numeric size does not answer a question about their widths.

sections.heading: Check a shoe measurement that has practical meaning
paragraphs: Start with a pair you own and know to fit. If it has a removable insole and you intend to compare insoles, measure the reference insole using the same method you request from the warehouse. Include where the heel and toe endpoints lie. A rounded toe means the longest point may sit away from the centre line. A curved insole laid against a straight ruler may produce a different result from a flexible tape following the curve. Name the method so the two numbers can be interpreted together.

Do not infer fit from an outsole measurement alone. Soles can extend well beyond the upper or curve upward at the toe, and different shapes make identical exterior lengths compatible with different internal spaces. A measurement can answer whether two received shoes differ visibly from each other, yet still leave your personal fit uncertain. Ask the seller for the relevant chart or last information if available and decide what level of uncertainty is acceptable before overseas shipping. A correct size label remains only one piece of the comparison.

sections.heading: Work through three common label conflicts
paragraphs: In the first case, both shoes match the selected variant but the carton identifies a different size. Ask whether the correct retail box is available if you need it for gifting or storage, and check whether a packaging mix-up suggests a wider matching problem. In the second case, the shoes agree with each other but both differ from the order. Confirm the size system and seller mapping, then request the relevant order remedy if the discrepancy remains. In the third case, the two shoes genuinely differ from one another. Document both labels together and avoid joining the pair to an international parcel until the issue has been addressed.

The requested response should match the case. A buyer who only needs a correct pair may accept an unrelated box if the shoes are verified. Someone who bought a collectible boxed set or a gift may care about both. For a mismatched left and right shoe, swapping a carton cannot resolve the issue. State which outcome you need and ask whether the seller can exchange the full pair or supply the correct component under its actual policy.

sections.heading: Verify a new pair independently
paragraphs: When a replacement arrives, repeat the label check using the new warehouse reference. Do not assume that a seller's agreement to exchange the product confirms the actual replacement. Match the new left and right labels, model, width and visible condition. If the retail packaging matters, inspect the new box record as well. Store the original discrepancy and its resolution separately so similar warehouse thumbnails cannot lead to shipment of the wrong entry.

For a shared order containing several pairs in neighboring sizes, create a simple allocation by order reference, recipient and specific variant. Confirm the allocation after replacement and before parcel submission. A matching carton can help organize the inventory, but the physical shoe labels are still the evidence that determines which pair belongs to whom. Once the box reaches the destination, retain the relevant labels until everyone has checked the contents against the agreed allocation.

sections.heading: If the ordered shoes are gifts for different people
paragraphs: Keep the recipients' own shoe measurements and preferred width separate. Two people who use the same numerical retail size may expect different internal space. When the warehouse holds several pairs, ask for photos that can be matched to their individual references. After delivery, keep the pairs and corresponding boxes together until each recipient has checked the labels. This simple inventory step avoids turning a household mix-up into a mistaken seller exchange request.

articles.title: Planning OOTDBuy warehouse storage when an order arrives in stages
articles.description: OOTDBUY publishes a storage help topic, and the relevant dates for a particular order belong in the account record.

sections.heading: Track the received pieces individually
paragraphs: OOTDBUY publishes a storage help topic, and the relevant dates for a particular order belong in the account record. Give each stored item its own line in your notes. Include the warehouse identifier, arrival date, displayed deadline and any open inspection question. Items bought together can reach the warehouse on different days and require separate decisions.

sections.heading: Work backward from the earliest deadline
paragraphs: If a wardrobe order includes a ready coat, a delayed belt and trousers needing a size check, start with the coat's actual deadline. Ask support what action is required before that time, including how an extension would be requested if available. Also check whether a seller return has its own earlier deadline. Keeping an item in storage and preserving its eligibility for a seller remedy involve different decisions.

sections.heading: Give waiting a price
paragraphs: Estimate what it would cost to ship the ready items alone and what dimensions the delayed piece might add. An inexpensive accessory can hold up a much larger order. Compare the possible freight saving with any verified extension cost, the uncertainty of the seller's dispatch date and whether you need the ready goods by a particular date. Treat all unconfirmed arrival dates as estimates.

sections.heading: Close the decision on the right record
paragraphs: When you decide to ship, confirm which warehouse identifiers are selected. If you arrange an extension, retain the confirmation and check that the displayed deadline changed for the intended item. If the seller agrees to exchange a piece, capture the status of that exchange before removing it from your notes. Storage planning works when every physical item ends with a recorded next action.

sections.heading: Use separate clocks for separate decisions
paragraphs: A storage date answers how long a warehouse entry can remain under its stated conditions. A seller remedy can depend on another event, and dispatch planning depends on a third timeline. Write the actual displayed date or event for each, including its time zone when available. For a ready coat with a possible missing button, resolve the seller question promptly even if the storage date looks distant. For an accepted item awaiting consolidation, the relevant question may be when you must choose a route or request an extension.

When two items appear to share a deadline, check the underlying entries. A package received by a domestic carrier on Friday and accepted into the agent's warehouse on Monday has at least two meaningful events. Copy the deadline the account actually attaches to the warehouse item. If it is ambiguous, ask which event controls and whether the displayed time is inclusive. Preserve any confirmation rather than setting a personal reminder from an unsupported assumption.

sections.heading: Plan for a seller who cannot give a dispatch date
paragraphs: Make a decision that works with the goods already available. Estimate a parcel containing just the ready pieces, and ask what happens if the missing item is canceled. If that plan fits your budget and timing, you have a real fallback while waiting for the seller's response. If the ready order makes sense only as a complete set, ask promptly about the available remedies and their deadlines. A delayed accessory can change whether the purchase meets its original purpose, even when the accessory itself cost very little.

sections.heading: Set up an inventory that matches the warehouse records
paragraphs: Give each physical warehouse entry a row rather than giving each marketplace transaction a row. One seller can send a purchase in parts, and two sellers can send items on the same day. For each entry, include its warehouse identifier, original seller order, option, received quantity, current status, deadline and planned action. If an entry represents a sealed set, describe what has been verified from the outside and which contents remain unconfirmed. This avoids assuming that a general received status has settled every quantity question.

Check which time zone appears on the relevant account screen. A date displayed without a time deserves clarification if you plan to take action close to the limit. Set your own reminder earlier than the final displayed date to allow time for a support reply, inspection request or parcel decision. The reminder is a planning choice and does not alter the platform's terms. Keep the current official storage guidance and your item-specific dates together, especially if another person is helping manage the order.

sections.heading: Plan around a replacement and its original item
paragraphs: An exchange can put two similar records into the same timeline. The original garment may still be visible in the order history while a replacement is in transit. Mark the original with the pending remedy and avoid treating its availability as permission to include it in a parcel. When the replacement arrives, give it a new line and record its actual displayed status and dates. Ask which record will be removed and whether you need to do anything further to preserve the seller arrangement.

Suppose a coat in storage needs a matching belt from a seller who cannot confirm stock. The buyer has three decisions: whether the coat itself is acceptable, whether the belt can still arrive within a useful time, and whether to store or ship the coat while waiting. Ask the seller about the belt independently and ask the agent about the coat's actual options. A seller promise to look for stock is not the same as dispatch confirmation, and it does not amend a warehouse deadline.

sections.heading: Compare the real cost of waiting
paragraphs: Write down a current quote for the goods you could ship immediately. Then estimate the outcome if the delayed items are included, using their likely packaging, destination and route. If a delayed item is rigid, its arrival could make the grouped box more expensive than the simple addition of its weight suggests. If it is small and soft, the marginal freight might be modest. Record the reason for your estimate rather than relying only on a total number with no physical assumptions.

Add any actual extension charge only after confirming what it covers, which item it applies to and the new deadline it would create. For an item with a verified seller defect, also consider the time available to seek a remedy and the cost of losing that option. An extension for warehouse space and a return window for a seller order can have different conditions. The cheapest storage plan can be poor value if it allows time-sensitive information or a seller remedy to expire unnoticed.

sections.heading: Coordinate a shared order
paragraphs: If two people are grouping goods, assign one person to monitor the actual warehouse deadlines and another, if needed, to collect outstanding seller information. Keep the same inventory visible to both. Record which buyer is willing to wait and which needs a parcel by a certain date. When someone asks for delay to add another item, describe what that means for the goods already received, including storage, delivery timing and any potential extra packing.

Before the agreed shipment date, review every row. Remove canceled items from the proposed parcel, exclude unresolved exchanges, and check that every item marked ready has actually been selected. Save the parcel confirmation and resulting tracking reference next to the included entries. For anything left behind, assign a new action date based on its actual record. The process is complete when the shipment and the remaining storage inventory both match the decisions the buyers made.

sections.heading: Create a handover note before travelling
paragraphs: If you will be unavailable near a storage deadline, leave a written decision for the person helping you. Identify the specific warehouse entry, outcome you authorize and any maximum extension or freight amount you have actually agreed to. A vague instruction to wait for the rest of the haul can leave them unable to act if the seller cannot dispatch. Preserve account security and use the platform's authorized processes for account actions. Even without account access, a helper can track reminders and gather the seller information you need.

articles.title: Preparing an OOTDBuy aftersales request for a short shipment
articles.description: An apparent shortage can come from a genuine packing error or a misunderstanding about what one selected unit contains.

sections.heading: Recount against the purchased unit
paragraphs: An apparent shortage can come from a genuine packing error or a misunderstanding about what one selected unit contains. Read the order confirmation and seller option together. If you ordered two packs of four coasters, your expected total is eight pieces. A warehouse photo showing two closed boxes establishes a box count only. Ask whether the individual contents can be checked without compromising the packaging.

sections.heading: Build a record the seller can follow
paragraphs: Keep the original selection, quantity, seller description and warehouse images in order. Write the discrepancy in one sentence using numbers: “Ordered two packs of four; the opened packs contain four and three.” Identify which pack is short if possible. Where the goods arrived under different domestic tracking numbers, confirm that no second parcel remains outstanding before requesting a remedy.

sections.heading: Ask for a defined outcome
paragraphs: OOTDBUY provides guidance for returns, refunds and applying for aftersales. Open the relevant record and ask whether the seller can supply the missing piece, replace a pack or accept another remedy. Include any alternative you would accept and ask about applicable costs and timing. A request for one replacement component may require a different process from returning both packs.

sections.heading: Protect the remaining options
paragraphs: Keep the goods and packaging in the condition requested by the agent while the seller reviews the case. Ask whether any deadline continues to run while waiting for a response. If a replacement is agreed, verify the final count against your initial order before submitting international freight. File the seller's reply with that order so the new arrival does not look like an unrelated extra piece.

sections.heading: Check whether a sealed pack can be counted
paragraphs: If a seller sells ten small parts in sealed pouches, a photo of one intact pouch cannot confirm its contents unless the parts are visible through the material. Ask whether the warehouse can count through the packaging or obtain the seller's packing record first. Breaking a seal can affect the item or the seller's willingness to accept a return. Before asking for an opened count, find out what opening would change. Where opening is permitted, request a full overview with pieces laid out in a way that makes the total unambiguous.

For mixed-color sets, count each variant separately. “Eight pieces received” may hide the fact that an order for four green and four blue pieces arrived as six green and two blue. In that situation the total quantity is correct while the variant mix is wrong. Name the discrepancy precisely and keep one photograph showing all pieces together, followed by any close-up needed to distinguish their markings.

sections.heading: Choose the smallest remedy that solves the problem
paragraphs: If seven of eight coasters arrived and the set will be gifted in its original packaging, one replacement sent later may pose a timing or packing problem. If the goods are for personal use, the same remedy may be perfectly acceptable. Tell the agent which outcome works before the seller proposes a solution. If the seller offers a partial refund, check the amount, currency, destination of the credit and what happens to the item in storage. If a replacement is offered, ask how it will be identified and whether you need to wait before submitting international freight.

sections.heading: Distinguish a short shipment from a misunderstood sales unit
paragraphs: Seller pages can group a single component, a sample and a full kit under one lead image. Begin by reopening the option actually purchased and reading the unit beside its price. If the line says one pair, identify which two pieces define that pair. If it says one set, look for a written contents list. A seller image showing a complete styled collection may illustrate possible choices without promising to send all pictured goods. Preserve the source selection and its original wording before comparing the warehouse result.

If the seller's words are ambiguous, ask for the specification for the selected option rather than quoting the broad product title. A rack shown with three hooks may sell the rack and hooks separately; an order for two units might therefore mean two racks without hooks. Conversely, if the written option promises a rack with three hooks, a missing hook is a concrete discrepancy. Use the most specific documented promise available and keep any seller confirmation that clarifies it.

sections.heading: Check split dispatch and warehouse grouping
paragraphs: A seller can ship one merchandise order in multiple cartons, and a warehouse can record one carton while another remains in transit. Ask for the seller's complete domestic dispatch list and reconcile each tracking number to the warehouse entry it reached. When two similar shipments arrive close together, match by seller and reference, not just by date or product image. A missing second shipment needs tracing; a physically received carton containing too few pieces needs a contents investigation. Keeping those scenarios separate saves time.

A large purchase may contain several inner packs in one outer carton. A photo of two inner boxes does not establish the units inside them if they are closed. See whether external markings identify the quantities and ask what inspection is available without damaging the packaging. If opening is necessary to settle the issue, clarify any consequences for intact seals, resale packaging or seller eligibility first. Do not ask someone to open a package purely for a better picture if that changes the remedy you need.

sections.heading: Ask for evidence that distinguishes the missing piece
paragraphs: For goods with multiple sizes or colors, organize the count by variant rather than by total. Eight replacement feet might all be present while two use the wrong thread. A row of similar parts in a photograph can hide the difference. Ask for the specific marking or dimensions that identify the disputed pair and a wider shot tying those pieces to the rest of the set. If necessary, annotate a copy to point out the exact feature; retain the original files separately.

Write a short account with four facts: what was ordered, what the seller confirmed, what was verified at intake and what remains missing or wrong. For example, “Order 123 calls for two sealed sets of four blue coasters. Two boxes arrived. One opened box contains four blue pieces, and the other contains three blue pieces. Please ask the seller how to supply the eighth coaster.” That statement identifies the actual remedy needed and leaves less room for an unhelpful reply about the number of boxes.

sections.heading: Follow the resolution into the final parcel
paragraphs: If the seller dispatches a missing component, obtain the new domestic tracking reference and record it under the initial shortage case. When it reaches the warehouse, confirm the variant and count. A small replacement can look like an unrelated order if it has no clear description. Ask how it will be packed with the original set and whether the packaging can still meet your intended use, particularly if the goods are gifts or belong to different recipients.

If the remedy is financial instead, verify the exact amount and where it was credited before closing the case. Update your inventory to show the actual number that will travel, since the original purchase record can continue to display the initial quantity. At delivery, count against the corrected inventory and retain the seller response. This prevents the same pre-shipment shortage from being reported later as a loss during international transport and makes any genuinely new discrepancy easier to identify.

sections.heading: When the seller supplies a different remedy
paragraphs: If a seller offers a substitute rather than the missing part, compare the substitute against the purpose of the set. A different-colored coaster may complete the numerical count while leaving a coordinated gift incomplete. Ask whether the replacement is an exact variant and record the seller's wording. If you accept a different component, amend the expected contents list before the overseas parcel is packed. Later, compare delivery against the agreement you actually made so an accepted substitution is not mistaken for another packing error.

articles.title: Recording a damaged OOTDBuy parcel when a fragile item arrives
articles.description: OOTDBUY lists separate help topics for fragile breakage, receipt information and compensation.

sections.heading: Document the parcel as received
paragraphs: OOTDBUY lists separate help topics for fragile breakage, receipt information and compensation. If you discover a crushed carton, photograph the exterior, shipping label and visible damage together before discarding anything. Capture all affected sides and enough of the entire box to show where each close-up belongs. Retain original files and avoid posting your unredacted address publicly.

sections.heading: Link outer damage to the packed item
paragraphs: As you unpack, record the padding and the item's position in the carton. A cracked ceramic handle directly beside a dented corner tells a different story from a small chip inside intact inner packaging. If sharp fragments are visible, avoid handling them to improve the picture. Document what can be seen safely and retain the packaging for the next instructions.

sections.heading: Distinguish packaging damage from product damage
paragraphs: A dented gift box, a scratched finish and a broken functional component produce different losses. State exactly which one you found. Compare the delivered item with the warehouse record and check whether its packaging already showed damage before dispatch. Where a set contains several pieces, count the affected pieces and identify the unbroken ones. Accurate scope helps support understand the claim.

sections.heading: Ask the right party within the applicable window
paragraphs: Open OOTDBUY's current receipt and compensation guidance and contact the official channel promptly with your parcel and order identifiers. Ask whether a carrier damage report, photos of the label or another document is required for your route. Retain any report reference. A well-documented claim still depends on the applicable conditions, so avoid discarding evidence until you receive instructions.

sections.heading: Keep the condition of each layer distinct
paragraphs: There are at least three possible layers to document: the shipping carton, the seller's retail box and the actual product. A bend in the outer carton may leave the product intact, while an undamaged carton can contain a ceramic handle broken before packing. Capture each layer in sequence and explain what you saw as it became visible. If the parcel contains multiple fragile pieces, place an undamaged piece beside the affected one only when doing so is safe and gives a useful scale comparison. Keep all original labels and major pieces in the positions you initially recorded.

Where a protective insert is part of the evidence, show how it fits the product. An empty-looking space close to a broken corner may help someone understand the packing, but it is not by itself proof of when the damage happened. Preserve the warehouse images and any packing instructions alongside the delivery photographs. Those records let the reviewer compare the item before dispatch and after arrival without relying on recollection.

sections.heading: Write a claim summary that can be checked
paragraphs: Start with the parcel number and delivery date. Identify the order and variant, name the affected component and make the scale of loss clear. “One of two cups has a detached handle; the second is intact” is easier to investigate than “the order arrived ruined.” Ask what time limit and documents apply to your route and whether the carrier needs to see the packaging. If a local carrier issues a damage report, keep the case reference and relevant correspondence with your OOTDBUY support request.

sections.heading: Create a photograph set with clear scale and context
paragraphs: Begin outside the parcel. Take one photograph in which the entire shipping carton is visible, then a closer view of the dent, puncture or wet area if present. Keep a clear photo of the label for the private support case and redact it before sharing elsewhere. If an edge has split, show where that edge sits relative to the rest of the box. A highly magnified picture of cardboard fibres may be difficult to interpret without a wider frame.

As each layer is removed, photograph the item in place when safe to do so. Include the inner retail box, protective insert and the corresponding area of the outer carton. A small undamaged section of the item can provide scale for a close-up, or you can place an ordinary ruler nearby if this does not require moving dangerous fragments. Save original files with descriptive names that identify the layer and order. A single edited collage can be convenient, but original photographs preserve detail and give the reviewer a clearer sequence.

sections.heading: Use the carrier's own document list where relevant
paragraphs: Carriers differ in how they handle damage enquiries. UPS, for instance, publishes guidance about supporting photographs, including the item and its packing, the outside of the parcel and the shipping label. That is a useful illustration of why preserving all layers matters. For an actual OOTDBUY shipment, check which carrier and service handled the route and what documents its current rules require. The party entitled to open the case can also depend on the service, so ask the agent which channel should submit it.

Keep evidence of the product itself as well as the carton. The seller order, actual paid amount, product description and pre-shipment warehouse photos help identify what was shipped and its earlier visible condition. For an item bought as part of a larger order, identify its individual value where documented. If you received two identical items and only one was damaged, state the quantity affected and keep photos that show both. A claim for the entire seller order could overstate the actual loss.

sections.heading: Distinguish observations from an explanation of cause
paragraphs: Write the timeline as observations: the carton arrived with a dented corner, the inner box had a mark on the corresponding side, and the handle was detached when opened. Those facts are observable. A conclusion about exactly when or by whom it was damaged requires additional evidence. If warehouse photos already showed a mark, include them so the reviewer can compare the stage at which the issue first became visible. Preserving an inconvenient detail can prevent an investigation being directed at the wrong party.

When the outer carton looks intact, document that too. Fragile components can move inside packaging, and the visible state of the exterior alone does not settle what happened. Ask whether the carrier or agent needs an inspection before anything is discarded or returned. If the damage creates a hazard, prioritize safe handling and describe what you could photograph without touching unsafe fragments. The purpose is to provide reliable evidence, not to recreate the original packing arrangement after the fact.

sections.heading: Keep the enquiry open until its disposition is clear
paragraphs: Record the time you first contacted the agent, any carrier report reference, the documents requested and the stated deadline for providing them. If you are waiting for a carrier reply, ask whether another action is needed with the agent in the meantime. Keep related messages in one case where possible. Starting a fresh conversation each time without the existing reference can make a single enquiry look like several unrelated reports.

If a remedy is offered, read its scope before accepting. A replacement, partial credit or reimbursement may address different parts of the loss. Check the affected quantity, whether the damaged item or packaging must be retained, where any credit goes and whether there is a further carrier step. Keep the written resolution and verify it appears in the relevant account or shipment record. Those final checks matter particularly when several gift items travelled in one box but only one suffered damage.

sections.heading: Verify replacement goods on their own terms
paragraphs: When a replacement fragile piece is sent, confirm that it matches the affected variant and will use a packing method appropriate to the original problem. Record whether the seller, agent or another party covers any specific transport cost before approving a new shipment. A replacement item and replacement freight can be separate parts of a resolution. Photograph the new arrival and close the original enquiry only when the agreed outcome is clear, or note exactly which part still awaits confirmation.

articles.title: Reconciling an OOTDBuy top-up with a product order
articles.description: OOTDBUY publishes separate help entries for top-up, PayPal and international credit cards.

sections.heading: Identify which balance changed
paragraphs: OOTDBUY publishes separate help entries for top-up, PayPal and international credit cards. A payment provider's confirmation tells you that a payment event occurred. To understand what it funded, compare it with the balance ledger and the order record in your OOTDBUY account. A balance increase, a merchandise payment and a parcel charge have different references and affect different amounts.

sections.heading: Make a simple ledger
paragraphs: For each event, write the time, original currency, amount, reference and resulting balance if displayed. In an illustrative account that starts at zero, a 200-unit credit followed by a 150-unit purchase would leave 50 units before any other lines. Keep conversion and provider charges as separate entries where shown. Mixing a dollar payment with a yuan wallet entry as though the numbers shared a unit makes the reconciliation meaningless.

sections.heading: Investigate an apparent duplicate
paragraphs: Match both provider events to their references and check their status. One may be pending while another is settled, or a top-up and a later order may have been recorded close together. If you cannot match the records, pause before repeating the transaction and request a reconciliation. Include the transaction reference and amount. Keep passwords, full card details and unrelated account activity out of the message.

sections.heading: Record the resolution
paragraphs: If support confirms a correction, check the account ledger, order status and provider history again. Retain the written response and any refund or adjustment reference. A wallet correction and a repayment to a card need different follow-up checks. Review the payment method and final currency displayed for the next order rather than assuming every method produces the same result.

sections.heading: Separate timing differences from accounting differences
paragraphs: A pending card authorization can appear before a provider posts its settled transaction. A wallet entry may also use the platform's account currency while the statement uses the card's billing currency. Compare status and currency before comparing the final digits. If you paid late at night, a provider and an account in different time zones can show adjacent dates for the same event. Use references and amounts to identify the event rather than assuming every same-day line has a matching payment.

Consider a hypothetical buyer who funds a balance, buys two items, then receives a partial adjustment for one canceled unit. The ledger should preserve a credit, the purchase or purchases and the later adjustment. If the buyer removes the canceled item from a spreadsheet and also subtracts the refund a second time, the remaining balance will appear wrong. Rebuild it from the opening balance by adding each recorded credit and subtracting each recorded debit once.

sections.heading: Send an enquiry that protects private information
paragraphs: Give support the order reference, provider transaction reference, original amount and currency, and the time of the payment. If a screenshot is needed, redact full card numbers, addresses and unrelated transactions. State what you can actually see: for instance, the provider marked the payment settled but the account still shows no matching credit. Ask support to identify which record it should match and the expected next action. A vague request about a missing payment may produce a reply about the wrong merchandise order or a separate parcel charge.

sections.heading: Reconstruct a payment with a running balance
paragraphs: Start from a balance you can independently see in the OOTDBUY account and list subsequent events in order. For each, enter the timestamp, type, order or provider reference, amount in the ledger currency and resulting balance. Keep a separate column for the amount and currency shown by the external provider. If the provider charges a card in a different currency from the wallet, the numbers should not be added together. The provider record documents the funding event while the platform ledger shows what happened to the funded balance.

Consider an illustrative wallet that begins with 20 units, receives 100, then pays 75 for a product and receives a 10-unit adjustment. Its resulting balance would be 55 units before any other transactions. An external receipt can show the funding payment without showing the subsequent internal purchase or adjustment. If you start at zero instead of the actual 20, the reconciliation will appear wrong even though every recorded event is otherwise consistent. Preserve the opening balance and the full event sequence.

sections.heading: Handle different transaction dates and states
paragraphs: A payment initiated late in the evening can appear under different calendar dates in the provider and platform records, particularly if they use different time zones. A pending authorization may also look like a second payment next to the settled transaction. Check whether the records share a provider reference, amount and currency and read the provider's actual status descriptions. Avoid treating every pending amount as a final debit or simply ignoring it because another amount seems familiar.

If the funding appears settled externally but no corresponding wallet credit is visible, check the account and payment identity used. Someone who has more than one login method or account can be looking at the wrong order history. Use official account recovery or support where needed; avoid sharing credentials to ask another person to search for the event. Give support the provider transaction reference and the platform account context that can identify the purchase, while omitting unrelated statement lines or private security details.

sections.heading: Separate a canceled purchase from its funding
paragraphs: When a seller cancels an order, distinguish the original top-up from the sale and the later adjustment. A return to the platform balance and a reversal to the outside payment method appear in different records. Read the actual resolution and ask where the refund will be sent if it is unclear. Then check the named destination and retain the new reference. Removing the canceled purchase from your spreadsheet without recording its adjustment loses the explanation for why the balance changed.

For a partial cancellation, use the product line actually affected. If a wallet paid for three items and one seller cannot supply an accessory, the adjustment may relate only to the accessory amount and any applicable charge. Compare the documented calculation with the order summary and ask about unexplained differences. Keep any international parcel payment separate, especially if the cancellation occurred before that parcel was created. The fact that two payments relate to the same shopping trip does not make them the same transaction.

sections.heading: Gather only evidence needed for support
paragraphs: Prepare a concise timeline with the original payment time, provider status, expected platform event and the specific event that is missing or surprising. Mark amounts with their currencies and include transaction references. A screenshot should show the relevant reference and amount without exposing your complete card number, address, account password or other people's transactions. If the case involves multiple purchases, identify the one that is unresolved and note which others already reconcile.

When a correction is confirmed, verify the updated balance or provider transaction and record when it appeared. If support says an action will happen later, ask which event will confirm completion and what reference to use if it does not appear. Keep the record until that outcome is visible. For future orders, capture the selected payment method, final currency and fee information at checkout rather than assuming the same method will always produce the same displayed amount or settlement path.

sections.heading: When a household shares purchase costs
paragraphs: Reconcile the platform transaction first, then decide how to divide it privately. A person who contributed to a top-up might have funded multiple items or left an unused balance. Allocate only the amount actually used for the agreed purchases, and record who owns any remaining credit. If a later refund is issued, use the documented item and destination of the refund to adjust the household calculation. This avoids treating unused wallet funds as a product cost or counting a single credit twice.
